slides.title: Influence Built Through Digital Platforms
bullets: DOL influence runs through social media, podcasts, video and blogs
LinkedIn and X are especially relevant platforms
This can operate instead of, or alongside, the traditional academic path
The traditional path relies on publications, congresses and guideline committees

slides.title: Digital Footprint Replaces Academic Standing
bullets: Follower counts on relevant platforms
Engagement rates on scientific content
Reach and resonance of posts discussing clinical topics
Depth of community interaction matters more than raw audience size

slides.title: From Global Voices to Micro-Influencers
bullets: Globally recognised clinical authorities with large, engaged followings
Micro-influencers with smaller but highly engaged niche audiences
Micro-influencer recommendations carry weight because the audience trusts them deeply

slides.title: KOL and DOL Status Often Overlap
bullets: Many senior academic KOLs have also built substantial digital followings
Many DOLs lack an equivalent traditional academic profile
Treating digital influence as a lesser, supplementary category is a mistake
Digital scientific exchange still follows the same compliance and balance standards

slides.title: Mapping Must Add a Digital Dimension
bullets: Identify the relevant DOLs in a territory
Understand which digital channels and communities actually shape local practice
Influence today is measured across both traditional and digital indicators

takeaway.title: DOLs shape clinical opinion through digital channels, not just academic ones
bullets: Follower reach, engagement quality and community trust are the key indicators
KOL and DOL status frequently overlap in the same person
Territory mapping must now explicitly include the digital dimension
takeaway.nextLesson: Differences between KOL, rising star, clinical champion and scientific influencer
